# MCP tool reference

<!-- Generated by backend/scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py from the source code. Do not edit by hand. -->

Stackpilot's built-in MCP server (`https://<your address>/mcp`, Streamable HTTP) offers **196 tools**: 101 read, 28 operate, 37 change and 30 destructive.

Every call goes through the same pipeline: the token or OAuth connection must hold the tool's **scope**, the call must stay inside the token's **customers**, the **policy** for the tool's **risk level** decides whether it runs, waits for approval or is blocked, and the call is written to the **AI activity log**. See [features](features.md#ai-gateway) for how policies work.

## Risk levels

| Risk | Meaning | Default policy |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 🟢 read | Look only: status, logs, lists | Run |
| 🔵 operate | Routine and easy to undo: restart, snapshot, refresh | Run |
| 🟠 change | Changes settings or creates things | Run |
| 🔴 destructive | Commands, updates, deletes, doors | Ask for approval |

Outside a customer's maintenance window, change and destructive calls ask for approval by default. A call with `dry_run` set counts as read.

## Scopes

Tick these per API token or OAuth connection. A tool marked *app-wide* works on the app itself or across customers and is refused for a token tied to specific customers.

| Scope | Allows |
| --- | --- |
| `read` | Read status, version, settings (without secrets), backups and audit log |
| `backups` | Run backups |
| `restore` | Restore a backup (destructive) |
| `updates` | Check for updates, switch channel and install updates |
| `settings` | Change mail settings and send test mail |
| `nodes` | Manage environments and nodes: pairing codes, CPU governor, notifications, agent updates |
| `node_updates` | Install package updates on nodes and reboot nodes |
| `logs` | Read logs (journal, Event Log, log files), service status, installed packages and files on nodes and servers |
| `services` | Start, stop and restart services on nodes and servers |
| `exec` | Run commands (shell or PowerShell) on nodes, servers and in containers as root/SYSTEM (every command is logged) |
| `copy` | Copy files and folders from one server to another |
| `guests` | Start, stop and restart VMs and containers, take snapshots, change CPU/memory |
| `guests_admin` | Create, delete and migrate VMs and containers, roll back snapshots, run community scripts |
| `templates` | Manage the container template library and push templates to nodes |
| `tasks` | Create, change and run scheduled tasks |
| `network` | Change bridges, firewall rules and SDN on Proxmox VE nodes (applied with backup and roll back) |
| `cluster` | Manage HA, replication, Proxmox backup jobs and storage |
| `restore_guests` | Restore VMs, containers and files from Proxmox VE backups (destructive, approval by default) |
| `deploy` | Deploy GitHub repositories into containers and change deployments |
| `unifi` | Read UniFi Network and Access: devices, clients, WiFi, firewall zones, events, doors and the access log |
| `unifi_admin` | UniFi Network actions: restart devices, power-cycle switch ports, authorize guests, switch WiFi on or off |
| `doors` | UniFi Access: unlock doors and change door lock rules (every action is logged) |
| `workstations` | Remote actions on workstations: Defender scans and signature updates, Group Policy refresh, messages to the user and logging users off |
| `reports` | Mail monthly customer reports to the customer's contacts |
| `runbooks` | Start runbooks, confirm their AI steps and create or change runbooks (every step keeps its own scope and guardrails) |
| `monitoring` | Create, change and delete uptime checks and set the uptime SLA of customers |
| `tickets` | Reply on customer tickets (mailed to the customer), add internal notes, change and open tickets |
| `docs` | Write customer documentation (pages are readable with the read scope) |
| `vault` | See the password vault (names, no secrets) and ask to use a credential: every use needs an admin's approval and is written to the vault's access log |
| `hub` | Use the tools of other MCP servers registered in the MCP hub (Keystone, GitHub, ...), within the guardrails |

## App: version and updates

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `get_system_info` | 🟢 read | `read` | Version, update channel (production/test), database and OS information of this app. | none |
| `check_for_updates` | 🟢 read | `read` | Ask GitHub whether a newer release exists on the current channel. | none |
| `set_update_channel` | 🟠 change | `updates` · app-wide | Switch between the 'production' (main branch) and 'test' (test branch) update channel. This does not install anything; use install_update afterwards. | `channel` |
| `install_update` | 🔴 destructive | `updates` · app-wide | Install release `tag` (for example v0.2.0 or v0.2.0-test.5). The app restarts. Set `confirm` to the same tag to confirm. A database dump is made first and the update is rolled back automatically if the new version does not start. | `tag`, `confirm` |
| `get_update_status` | 🟢 read | `read` | Progress of a running or the last update. | none |

## App: backups

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list_backup_targets` | 🟢 read | `read` · app-wide | Remote backup locations (FTP, FTPS, SFTP, SCP) with their schedules. Secrets are never returned. | none |
| `list_backup_runs` | 🟢 read | `read` · app-wide | Recent backup and restore runs with status, size and errors. | `limit`? |
| `list_remote_backups` | 🟢 read | `read` · app-wide | Backups that exist on a remote location (the source for restores). | `target_id` |
| `run_backup` | 🔵 operate | `backups` · app-wide | Start a backup now. kind: 'full', 'incremental' or 'auto' (incremental when a full exists). Returns when the backup has finished. | `target_id`, `kind`? |
| `restore_backup` | 🔴 destructive | `restore` · app-wide | Replace ALL current app data with backup `backup_id` from `target_id`. Set `confirm` to the backup_id to confirm. Always ask the user first. | `target_id`, `backup_id`, `confirm` |

## Customers and Proxmox nodes

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `get_overview` | 🟢 read | `read` | Environments, all machines with an agent (Proxmox VE nodes and standalone Linux/Windows servers: online, CPU/RAM/disk, pending updates, agent version) and totals. `customer` (name or id) limits it to one customer. `list_servers` gives the standalone servers in more detail. | `customer`? |
| `list_customers` | 🟢 read | `read` | All customers you may see (Home is a customer too): status (ok, attention, empty), machines online, Proxmox VE nodes, servers and workstations, pending updates, open alerts, UniFi devices and firmware updates, maintenance window and SLA. Start here when the user names a customer. | none |
| `get_customer_overview` | 🟢 read | `read` | Everything at one customer in one call: the customer context (notes for you, maintenance window, SLA, contacts), every machine (Proxmox VE nodes, servers, workstations) with status, OS, CPU/RAM, pending updates and what needs attention, UniFi connections, open alerts and totals. Read the notes and respect the maintenance window before changing anything. | `customer` |
| `optimisation_scan` | 🟢 read | `read` | "What can be optimised at customer X": one call that checks capacity (memory per node and the balance inside a cluster, with a guest to move), storage and SMART health, disks of servers and containers, pending updates and reboots, old agents, failed services, stopped guests, UniFi devices offline, firmware updates and (live) whether the guest WiFi is isolated from the LAN. Returns findings by severity with a suggestion and the tool to use next. Present them to the user and ask before acting; plan changes in the maintenance window. | `customer`, `live_network_checks`? |
| `get_morning_summary` | 🟢 read | `read` | The morning summary of the nightly checks: per customer the findings of last night (updates, security updates with the CVEs they fix, full disks, certificates that expire, failed or missing backups and the optimisation scan), what is new since the night before, what was resolved, and the proposals that wait for one click in Stackpilot (approval requests; changes wait for the customer's maintenance window). Tell the user what needs attention; an admin approves the proposals in the app (Morning summary or Approvals), not you. | `customer`?, `only_new`? |
| `run_nightly_checks` | 🔵 operate | `read` | Run the nightly checks now (normally they run every night), for all customers or one. They refresh the update lists and the backup coverage, check certificates and look up CVEs, and create proposals that an admin approves. Takes a few minutes; then read get_morning_summary. | `customer`? |
| `get_customer_context` | 🟢 read | `read` | The customer's notes for you, maintenance window, SLA and contacts (also available as the MCP resource stackpilot://customers/<id>). Follow the notes, e.g. "never restart X during office hours". | `customer` |
| `create_customer` | 🟠 change | `nodes` · app-wide | Create a customer. kind: 'home' (your own environment) or 'customer'. maintenance_window e.g. 'Tue 22:00-02:00'. notes: guidance for the AI and the team. | `name`, `kind`?, `description`?, `contact_name`?, `contact_email`?, `contact_phone`?, `maintenance_window`?, `sla`?, `notes`? |
| `update_customer` | 🟠 change | `nodes` | Change a customer's details. Only the fields you pass change. `append_note` adds a line to the notes (e.g. something the user asked you to remember about this customer); `notes` replaces them. | `customer`, `description`?, `contact_name`?, `contact_email`?, `contact_phone`?, `maintenance_window`?, `sla`?, `notes`?, `append_note`? |
| `list_nodes` | 🟢 read | `read` | Nodes with status, metrics, cluster, agent version and number of pending updates. | `customer`? |
| `get_node` | 🟢 read | `read` | Full details of one node, including the list of pending package updates. | `node` |
| `create_pairing_code` | 🔵 operate | `nodes` | Create a one-time pairing code (valid 24 hours) for a customer and the install command to run on a new machine. role: 'server' or 'workstation' (a PC or laptop) for Linux/Windows machines. | `customer`, `label`?, `role`? |
| `refresh_node_updates` | 🔵 operate | `nodes` | Run apt update on the node and return the list of upgradable packages. | `node` |
| `install_node_updates` | 🔴 destructive | `node_updates` | Install all pending updates on a node or server: apt dist-upgrade (Debian, Ubuntu, Proxmox VE), dnf upgrade (RHEL family) or Windows Update. Set `confirm` to the machine's name. Returns a job; follow it with get_node_job. Windows may need a reboot afterwards (reboot_node). | `node`, `confirm` |
| `reboot_node` | 🔴 destructive | `node_updates` | Reboot a node or server (Linux or Windows). On Proxmox VE running guests are handled by its own shutdown policy. Set `confirm` to the machine's name. Always ask the user first. | `node`, `confirm` |
| `get_node_job` | 🟢 read | `read` | Status and output of a node job (package upgrade, agent update). | `job_id` |
| `set_cpu_governor` | 🔵 operate | `nodes` | Set the CPU frequency governor (e.g. performance, schedutil, powersave). It is stored and applied again after every reboot. | `node`, `governor` |
| `get_customer_notifications` | 🟢 read | `read` | The Proxmox VE notification mail settings of a customer (password never returned). | `customer` |
| `update_customer_notifications` | 🟠 change | `nodes` | Set who gets Proxmox VE notifications for a customer and push them to its nodes. types: vzdump, replication, fencing, package-updates, system-mail. severities: info, notice, warning, error, unknown. use_app_smtp sends through the app's own mail server; a different SMTP server can only be entered in the web interface. | `customer`, `enabled`, `mailto`, `types`?, `severities`?, `use_app_smtp`? |
| `send_node_test_notification` | 🔵 operate | `nodes` | Let Proxmox VE on this node send a test notification through the pushed mail settings. | `node` |
| `update_node_agent` | 🔵 operate | `nodes` | Update the agent on the node to the version shipped with this app. | `node` |

## Server administration (logs, services, packages, files, commands)

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `read_logs` | 🟢 read | `logs` | Read the systemd journal of a Linux machine, or the Windows Event Log (System + Application) of a Windows server. unit: e.g. 'nginx' or 'pveproxy' (on Windows: the event source, e.g. 'Service Control Manager'). since/until: '1 hour ago', '2 days ago', 'today' or '2026-11-22 09:00'. priority: emerg, alert, crit, err, warning, notice, info or debug (that level and worse). grep: case-insensitive text/regex filter. Max 5000 lines. | `node`, `unit`?, `since`?, `until`?, `priority`?, `grep`?, `lines`?, `this_boot`? |
| `list_services` | 🟢 read | `logs` | Services on a node or server (systemd, or Windows services). state: 'failed' or 'running' to filter. On Windows 'failed' means an automatic service that stopped with an error. | `node`, `state`? |
| `get_service_status` | 🟢 read | `logs` | Status of one service: `systemctl status` plus properties on Linux; state, start mode, account, path and recent Service Control Manager events on Windows. | `node`, `unit` |
| `manage_service` | 🔵 operate | `services` | start, stop, restart, reload, enable or disable a service (systemd or Windows; on Windows enable = automatic start, no reload). `reason` is stored in the audit log. Ask the user before stopping or restarting production services. | `node`, `unit`, `action`, `reason` |
| `find_packages` | 🟢 read | `logs` | Which machines have a package installed and which version, e.g. 'nginx*' or 'openssl': dpkg/rpm/apk packages on Linux, installed programs on Windows ('*sql server*'), hotfixes with 'KB5*'. Shows whether an update is pending for it. Offline machines are listed without data. To mark versions as vulnerable or fixed for a CVE use `check_cve`. | `pattern`, `customer`? |
| `read_file` | 🟢 read | `logs` | Read a text file (or list a directory) on a machine, e.g. /etc/nginx/nginx.conf, /var/log/syslog with tail=true, or C:\inetpub\logs\LogFiles on Windows. At most 1 MiB. | `node`, `path`, `max_bytes`?, `tail`? |
| `run_command` | 🔴 destructive | `exec` | Run a command on a machine and return exit code, stdout and stderr (max 256 KiB each): /bin/sh as root on Linux, Windows PowerShell 5.1 as SYSTEM on Windows. `reason` is stored in the audit log with the command and its output. Prefer the read-only tools when they suffice, and ask the user before changing anything. timeout: seconds, max 1800. | `node`, `command`, `reason`, `timeout`? |

## Stand-alone servers and troubleshooting

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list_servers` | 🟢 read | `read` | Standalone Linux and Windows servers with an agent (not the Proxmox VE nodes): OS and version, online, CPU/RAM/disks, failed services, pending updates and what needs attention (offline, failed_services, disk_full, memory, reboot_required). os: 'linux' or 'windows'. | `customer`?, `os`? |
| `diagnose_server` | 🟢 read | `logs` | Health check of one machine in a single call: findings (full disks, memory, load, failed services, clock, pending updates/reboot), CPU/RAM/disks, failed services, error log lines of the last hour, busiest processes (CPU and memory), listening ports and time sync. Start here when something "doesn't work" on a server, then dig deeper with read_logs, get_service_status or search_logs. | `server` |
| `search_logs` | 🟢 read | `logs` | Search the logs of many machines at once (all machines when `servers` and `customer` are empty; os: linux, windows or proxmox). pattern: case-insensitive regex, e.g. 'postfix.*reject' or 'disk full\|No space left'. source: auto (systemd journal on Linux, Event Log on Windows), journal, eventlog or files (text log files: `paths` such as /var/log/nginx/*.log or C:\inetpub\logs\LogFiles; /var/log when empty). since: '1 hour ago', '2 days ago', 'today'. unit: systemd unit or Windows event source. priority: err, warning, ... log: Windows log names (e.g. 'System,Application,Security'). lines: max results per machine. | `pattern`, `servers`?, `customer`?, `os`?, `since`?, `source`?, `unit`?, `priority`?, `paths`?, `lines`?, `log`? |
| `read_event_log` | 🟢 read | `logs` | Windows Event Log entries of one Windows server as structured data (time, log, level, provider, event id, message). log: comma separated, e.g. 'System', 'Application', 'Security' or 'Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational'. level: critical, error, warning or information (that level and worse). source: event provider, e.g. 'Service Control Manager' or 'MSSQLSERVER'. | `server`, `log`?, `level`?, `since`?, `source`?, `grep`?, `max_events`? |
| `find_errors` | 🟢 read | `logs` | What is wrong where: per machine the failed services, the number of error log lines since `since` with the most recent ones, full disks and other findings, most broken machines first. Covers all machines when `servers` and `customer` are empty. | `servers`?, `customer`?, `os`?, `since`? |
| `check_cve` | 🟢 read | `logs` | Check a vulnerable package on all machines (or the given ones): the installed version per machine and, with `fixed_version` (the first fixed version from the advisory or the distribution's security tracker, e.g. '1.26.3-3' for Debian's nginx), whether it is still vulnerable and whether a pending update fixes it. package: name or glob ('nginx*', 'openssl', '*7-zip*' on Windows). Most affected machines first. Install fixes with install_node_updates. | `package`, `fixed_version`?, `servers`?, `customer`?, `os`? |
| `copy_data` | 🔴 destructive | `copy` | Copy files or folders from one machine to another (Linux and Windows, also between them), relayed through the app over the agents' encrypted connections; nothing is opened between the servers. paths: absolute paths on the source (max 20); each one is placed inside `target_path` (created when missing), like `cp -a <path> <target_path>/`. Owners, modes and times are kept on Linux. overwrite=false stops at the first existing file. `reason` is stored in the audit log. Returns a transfer; follow it with get_transfer. Ask the user before overwriting anything. | `source`, `paths`, `target`, `target_path`, `reason`, `overwrite`? |
| `get_transfer` | 🟢 read | `read` | Status of a data copy (stage send/receive/done, files, bytes, error) and the output of its two jobs (source and target). | `transfer_id` |

| `list_guests` | 🟢 read | `read` | VMs (type 'qemu') and containers (type 'lxc') on all Proxmox VE nodes: VMID, name, status, node, CPU/memory/disk use, tags. | `delete_guest` | 🔴 destructive | `guests_admin` | Delete a stopped VM or container including its disks. Cannot be undone. Set `confirm` to the guest's name. Always ask the user first. | `guest`, `confirm`, `node`? |
| `suggest_node` | 🟢 read | `read` | The least loaded online Proxmox VE node (memory 60 %, CPU 40 %), with the ranking. | `customer`? |
| `get_node_resources` | 🟢 read | `read` | Storages (with free space), network bridges, ISO images, templates and the next free VMID on a node: what you need to create a guest. | `node` |

A template that is not on the node yet is downloaded first. Returns a job. | `name`, `template`, `node`?, `cores`?, `memory_mb`?, `disk_gb`?, `storage`?, `bridge`?, `vlan`?, `ip`?, `gateway`?, `password`?, `ssh_key`?, `unprivileged`?, `start`?, `tags`?, `vmid`? |
| `create_vm` | 🟠 change | `guests_admin` | Create a VM. source 'iso': install from `iso` (volid, see get_node_resources) or `iso_url` (downloaded first). source 'cloud': a ready cloud image with cloud-init: `cloud_image` is one of debian-13, debian-12, ubuntu-24.04, ubuntu-22.04, rocky-9 (or give `cloud_url`), with `ci_user` and `ci_password` or `ssh_key`. ostype: l26, win11, win10, other. Returns a job. | `name`, `source`, `node`?, `iso`?, `iso_url`?, `cloud_image`?, `cloud_url`?, `cores`?, `memory_mb`?, `disk_gb`?, `storage`?, `bridge`?, `vlan`?, `ip`?, `gateway`?, `ostype`?, `ci_user`?, `ci_password`?, `ssh_key`?, `start`?, `vmid`? |
| `run_in_container` | 🔴 destructive | `exec` | Run a shell command as root inside a running container (pct exec ... sh -c) and return exit code and output. `reason` is stored in the audit log. Ask the user before changing anything. | `guest`, `command`, `reason`, `timeout`?, `node`? |

## Templates and community scripts

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list_templates` | 🟢 read | `read` | The container template library (official Proxmox VE and custom templates) with the status per node: current, outdated or missing. | none |
| `list_template_catalog` | 🟢 read | `read` | Official templates available from Proxmox VE (the pveam index) that can be added. | `query`? |
| `add_official_template` | 🟠 change | `templates` · app-wide | Add an official template (file name from list_template_catalog) to the library. With `sync` it is pushed to all nodes by the nightly sync (or run sync_templates now). | `filename`, `sync`? |
| `sync_templates` | 🔵 operate | `templates` · app-wide | Push the library to all online nodes now (or only one `template`). Returns a run id; follow it with get_task_run. | `template`? |
| `list_community_scripts` | 🟢 read | `read` | Scripts from community-scripts.org (synced nightly): slug, name, kind ('ct' container or 'vm'), default CPU/RAM/disk and OS. Use `query` to search (e.g. 'jellyfin', 'home assistant'). | `query`?, `kind`? |
| `get_community_script` | 🟢 read | `read` | The current text of a community script from the official repository (and the install part it loads) with its sha256. Show the user what it does before install_community_script. | `slug` |
| `install_community_script` | 🔴 destructive | `guests_admin` | Run a community script unattended ('Default' mode) as root on a Proxmox VE node; it creates the container/VM and installs the app. `sha256` must be the value from get_community_script (proves the script was reviewed). Without `node` the least loaded node is used. Ask the user first. Returns a job with the full log. | `slug`, `sha256`, `node`?, `hostname`?, `cpu`?, `ram_mb`?, `disk_gb`?, `storage`?, `bridge`?, `vlan`?, `ip`?, `gateway`? |

## Scheduled tasks

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list_scheduled_tasks` | 🟢 read | `read` · app-wide | Scheduled tasks (updates in containers, node updates, template sync, custom commands) with schedule, targets, options, last and next run. | none |
| `save_scheduled_task` | 🟠 change | `tasks` · app-wide | Create (or with `task_id` change) a scheduled task. kind: ct_community_update (the 'update' command of community-script containers), ct_apt_upgrade (apt-get update + full-upgrade, or apk/dnf, in containers), node_updates, template_sync, custom_command. cron: 5 fields in the app's time zone, e.g. '0 4 * * 0'. targets: {"scope": "all"\|"environments"\|"nodes"\|"guests"\|"tag", "environment_ids": [...], "node_ids": [...], "guests": [{"node_id": ..., "vmid": ...}], "tag": "...", "exclude_vmids": [...]}. options: {"snapshot": true, "rollback": true, "keep_snapshots": 3, "command": "...", "command_windows": "...", "run_on": "ct"\|"node", "timeout": 3600}. For custom_command on machines (run_on "node"), `command` is a bash script for Linux machines and `command_windows` a PowerShell script for Windows servers and workstations (it runs as LocalSystem); a machine only runs the script of its own OS. mail_on: always, failure or never. | `name`, `kind`, `cron`, `targets`?, `options`?, `mail_to`?, `mail_on`?, `enabled`?, `task_id`? |
| `delete_scheduled_task` | 🔴 destructive | `tasks` · app-wide | Delete a scheduled task. Set `confirm` to its name. | `task_id`, `confirm` |
| `run_scheduled_task` | 🔵 operate | `tasks` · app-wide | Run a scheduled task now. Returns a run id; follow it with get_task_run. | `task_id` |
| `get_task_run` | 🟢 read | `read` · app-wide | A run of a scheduled task or template sync with the result per target (snapshot, rolled back, error, last output lines). Without run_id: the last 10 runs (optionally of one task). | `run_id`?, `task_id`? |

| `list_backup_coverage` | 🟢 read | `read` | Backup coverage of a customer: every Proxmox VE guest, server and workstation with its status (ok, stale, failed, no_job, never, none, external, backup_server, excluded, not_monitored), last backup, age in hours, size, the jobs that cover it, the storages and the last error; plus the backup jobs, backup storages, Proxmox Backup Servers and the customer's backup policy (SLA). | `list_guest_backups` | 🟢 read | `read` | All backups of one VM or container on every backup storage of its cluster (Proxmox Backup Server included), newest first: volume id, time, size, storage, verification state, notes. | `backup_guest_now` | 🔵 operate | `cluster` | Make a one-off backup of a VM or container now (vzdump to `storage`, a backup storage of its cluster), outside the backup jobs; `protected` keeps it from being pruned. Follow the job with get_node_job. | `guest`, `storage`, `node`?, `mode`?, `protected`? |
| `restore_guest` | 🔴 destructive | `restore_guests` | Restore a backup (volume id from list_guest_backups or list_backup_coverage) as a VM or container on `node`. By default as a NEW guest with a free VMID (or `vmid`) next to the original; `overwrite=true` replaces the existing guest with that VMID (it must be stopped). A container needs `storage` for its disks unless it is overwritten; `unique` gives a copy new MAC addresses. Set `confirm` to the VMID that is overwritten, or to 'new' for a new guest. Always ask the user first; the AI gateway asks an admin's approval by default. Follow the job with get_node_job. | `node`, `volume`, `confirm`, `vmid`?, `storage`?, `overwrite`?, `start`?, `unique`? |
| `list_backup_files` | 🟢 read | `restore_guests` | Browse the files inside a backup on a Proxmox Backup Server (file-level restore), through the Proxmox VE `node`. | `restore_files` | 🟠 change | `restore_guests` | Extract a file or folder from a Proxmox Backup Server backup (path from list_backup_files) into a new folder on the Proxmox VE `node` (default /var/lib/stackpilot-restore/<time>); nothing existing is overwritten. | `add_storage` | 🟠 change | `cluster` | Add a storage to the cluster: dir (path), nfs (server, export), cifs (server, share, username, password) or pbs (server, datastore, username, password, fingerprint). | `node`, `storage`, `type`, `content`?, `path`?, `server`?, `export`?, `share`?, `username`?, `password`?, `datastore`?, `fingerprint`? |

| `find_software` | 🟢 read | `read` | Which workstations (and with include_servers also servers) have a program installed, with the version: e.g. 'teamviewer', 'office', 'chrome', '7-zip*'. Searches the stored inventories, so it also finds machines that are offline now. For a CVE on servers use check_cve. | `name`, `customer`?, `include_servers`? |
| `workstation_action` | 🔵 operate | `workstations` | Remote action on a workstation through the agent. action: defender_quick_scan or defender_full_scan (starts a Microsoft Defender scan in the background), defender_update (update the virus signatures), gpupdate (refresh Group Policy) or message (show `message` to the logged-in user(s); on Linux through wall). Windows only, except message. Give a short `reason`. Restarts go through reboot_node, updates through install_node_updates. | `workstation`, `action`, `reason`, `message`? |
| `log_off_workstation_user` | 🔴 destructive | `workstations` | Log a user off a workstation (all their sessions; unsaved work is lost). confirm must be the workstation's exact name. Ask the user first. | `workstation`, `user`, `confirm`, `reason` |

## monthly customer reports (phase 10)

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `get_customer_report` | 🟢 read | `read` | The monthly IT report of a customer: availability per server, incidents, updates installed and pending, Proxmox backups, workstations with their security status, security points, what the AI did (audit log, approvals) and recommendations. period: 'YYYY-MM' (default: the latest report). With generate=true a fresh report is made for the period (default: the current month so far), without mailing it. Returns the report data and the link to the PDF in Stackpilot. | `customer`, `period`?, `generate`?, `lang`? |
| `send_customer_report` | 🔵 operate | `reports` | Mail the customer's report (PDF and HTML attached) to the report recipients of the customer, or to `to`. period 'YYYY-MM': the latest report of that month, made when there is none (default: last month). This sends mail outside Stackpilot: ask the user first. | `customer`, `period`?, `to`? |

## Runbooks

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list_runbooks` | 🟢 read | `read` | The runbooks (fixed procedures such as "patch a server", "new employee", "new project via GitHub"): name, category, customer (none = for every customer), parameters and steps. Run one with run_runbook instead of doing the steps yourself: Stackpilot runs them in order, asks approval where the policy or the runbook says so and keeps the audit trail. | `customer`? |
| `get_runbook` | 🟢 read | `read` | One runbook (id or exact name) with all steps, their arguments and placeholders. | `runbook` |
| `run_runbook` | 🔵 operate | `runbooks` | Start a runbook (id or exact name) for a customer with its parameters. Stackpilot runs the steps one by one with this token's rights; steps that need approval wait for an admin (app and mail), changes outside the maintenance window wait for it, and manual steps wait for a person. Returns the run; follow it with get_runbook_run. Ask the user before starting a runbook that changes something, and give a short `reason`. | `runbook`, `reason`, `customer`?, `params`? |
| `get_runbook_run` | 🟢 read | `read` | The state of a runbook run: status (running, waiting_approval, waiting_input, succeeded, failed, cancelled) and per step its status, approval request, result or error. A manual step for the AI (assignee "ai") waits for complete_runbook_step. | `run_id` |
| `list_runbook_runs` | 🟢 read | `read` | Recent runbook runs (newest first), optionally of one customer or runbook, or only the ones that are not finished. | `customer`?, `runbook`?, `active_only`?, `limit`? |
| `complete_runbook_step` | 🔵 operate | `runbooks` | Confirm the manual step a run waits for, when that step is for the AI (assignee "ai"): you did what its instructions say (with other tools). `note` says what you did or found. failed=true stops the run (unless the step may fail). Steps for a person are confirmed in Stackpilot. | `run_id`, `note`, `failed`? |
| `cancel_runbook_run` | 🔵 operate | `runbooks` | Cancel a runbook run that is not finished: its open approval requests are withdrawn and no further steps run. Steps that already ran are not undone. | `run_id`, `reason` |
| `save_runbook` | 🟠 change | `runbooks` | Create a runbook, or change one (`runbook` = its id or name). steps: [{"id", "title", "kind": "tool"\|"manual"\|"wait", "tool", "args", "approval": "policy"\|"always", "on_failure": "stop"\|"continue", "optional", "wait_for_job", "instructions", "assignee": "human"\|"ai", "minutes"}]. params: [{"name", "label", "required", "default"}]. Arguments may use {{params.x}}, {{customer.name}}, {{customer.id}}, {{run.id}} and {{steps.<id>.result.<path>}}. category: maintenance, onboarding, project, remediation or other. customer: none = for every customer. Show the user the steps before saving. | `name`, `steps`, `params`?, `description`?, `category`?, `customer`?, `runbook`?, `enabled`?, `use_window`? |
| `delete_runbook` | 🔴 destructive | `runbooks` | Delete a runbook (its past runs stay in the history). Set `confirm` to the runbook's name. | `runbook`, `confirm` |

## Automatic recovery

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cleanup_disk` | 🔵 operate | `services` | Free disk space on a machine, safely: package caches, journal entries older than 14 days and temp files older than 7 days (Linux); temp files, the Windows Update download cache and the component store (Windows). Shows the disk use before and after. | `node`, `reason` |
| `recover_agent` | 🔵 operate | `services` | Bring back the agent of a server that runs as a VM or container on a Proxmox VE node that Stackpilot reaches: starts the guest when it is stopped, otherwise restarts the agent service inside it (pct exec, or the QEMU guest agent for a VM). Never on a Proxmox VE node itself. | `node`, `reason` |
| `list_network_adapters` | 🟢 read | `read` | The physical network adapters of a machine (Windows or Linux) with their link state: up, down (no link), disabled (switched off) or absent, plus description, speed and MAC address. | `node` |
| `restart_network_adapter` | 🔵 operate | `services` | Restart a network adapter that has no link (for example an uplink or X710 port that stayed down after a switch reboot): Restart-NetAdapter on Windows, ip link down/up on Linux, then wait up to a minute for the link. `adapter` is the exact name from list_network_adapters. An adapter that is up, switched off or absent is left alone, unless `force` is true and `confirm` equals the machine name (restarting an adapter that is up interrupts its traffic). | `node`, `adapter`, `reason`, `force`?, `confirm`? |
| `get_remediation` | 🟢 read | `read` | Automatic recovery: whether it is on or stopped (emergency stop), its limits, the rules (problem -> runbook, mode auto/approve/notify) and the latest attempts with their outcome (succeeded = the problem is gone, failed, waiting_approval, skipped by the loop protection). | `customer`?, `limit`? |
| `save_remediation_rule` | 🟠 change | `runbooks` | Create or change (`rule` = its id) an automatic recovery rule: when a problem shows up, Stackpilot runs `runbook` (id or exact name) within the policy. trigger "alert" with match {"kinds": [offline\|service\|network\|disk\|storage\|memory\|cpu\|smart\|unifi\|backup], "services": [units to watch, for "service"], "adapters": [names or descriptions with * ?, for "network"; empty = every wired physical adapter that was up], "local": true (network: the agent also restarts the adapter itself when it cannot reach Stackpilot), "machine": "web*", "machine_types": [server\|workstation\|proxmox]} or trigger "finding" with match {"codes": ["disk_full", "agent_old", ...]}. params fill in the runbook's parameters and may use {{machine.name}}, {{alert.detail.service}}, {{alert.detail.adapter}}, {{finding.params.x}} and {{customer.name}}. mode: auto, approve (every change asks an admin) or notify (only report). Show the user the rule before saving. | `name`, `trigger`, `match`, `runbook`, `params`?, `mode`?, `customer`?, `rule`?, `enabled`?, `delay_minutes`?, `cooldown_minutes`?, `max_attempts`?, `description`? |
| `delete_remediation_rule` | 🔴 destructive | `runbooks` | Delete an automatic recovery rule (its past attempts stay). Set `confirm` to the rule's name. | `rule`, `confirm` |
| `pause_remediation` | 🔵 operate | `runbooks` · app-wide | The emergency stop of automatic recovery: paused=true stops it for every customer and cancels the recoveries that are busy (steps that already ran are not undone); paused=false resumes it. Give a short `reason`. | `paused`, `reason` |

## Uptime and SLA

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list_uptime_checks` | 🟢 read | `read` | The uptime checks (websites, TCP ports, ping, DNS records, VPN endpoints) with their status (up, down, degraded = slower than its limit, unknown, paused), last response time and error, availability over 24 hours, 7 and 30 days and the certificate expiry of HTTPS and SSL VPN checks. `customer` limits to one customer; `status` to one status (for "is everything up": status=down). | `customer`?, `status`? |
| `get_uptime_check` | 🟢 read | `read` | One uptime check (id or exact name) with its response times over `range` (24h, 7d, 30d), the last 30 results with their errors and the incidents (when it was down and why). | `check`, `range`? |
| `save_uptime_check` | 🟠 change | `monitoring` | Create or change (`check` = its id or name) an uptime check for a customer. kind: http (target a URL; config {"method": GET\|HEAD, "expect_status": "200-399", "keyword": "text that must be on the page", "keyword_absent": false, "verify_tls": true, "follow_redirects": true}), tcp (target a host, `port`), ping (a host), dns (target the name; config {"record_type": A\|AAAA\|CNAME\|MX\|TXT\|NS\| SOA\|CAA\|SRV\|PTR, "expect": "value that must be in the answer", "server": "resolver IP"}) or vpn (config {"mode": "ssl"} = the VPN portal answers TLS on `port` (443), {"mode": "tunnel"} = a host behind the tunnel answers ping). `probe`: run the check from this machine's agent (name or id, at the same customer) instead of from Stackpilot, for internal addresses and tunnels. `machine`: the machine the service runs on, so alerts belong to it and automatic recovery can act on them. Down after `fail_after` failed runs in a row; `slow_ms` makes it "degraded" (warning) above that time. `in_sla`: counts towards the customer's uptime SLA. Show the user the check before saving. | `customer`, `name`, `kind`, `target`, `port`?, `config`?, `check`?, `probe`?, `machine`?, `enabled`?, `interval_seconds`?, `timeout_seconds`?, `fail_after`?, `slow_ms`?, `cert_warn_days`?, `severity`?, `in_sla`? |
| `delete_uptime_check` | 🔴 destructive | `monitoring` | Delete an uptime check with its history and incidents (they no longer count in the SLA). Set `confirm` to the check's name. To stop checking for a while, save it with enabled=false instead. | `check`, `confirm` |
| `run_uptime_check` | 🟢 read | `read` | Run an uptime check now (instead of waiting for its interval) and return the result: ok, the response time, HTTP status, error and the new status of the check. | `check` |
| `get_sla_report` | 🟢 read | `read` | The uptime SLA per customer for a month (period 'YYYY-MM', default: this month so far): the measured availability of the checks that count in the SLA, the target (the customer's uptime SLA setting, or a percentage in its SLA text), met or not, the downtime against the allowed downtime, and per check its availability and incidents. Downtime inside the maintenance window does not count unless the customer's setting says so. With `customer` also the incidents. | `customer`?, `period`? |
| `set_uptime_sla` | 🟠 change | `monitoring` | Set the uptime SLA of a customer: `target_pct` (for example 99.9; clear_target=true removes it, then a percentage in the customer's SLA text is used), `exclude_maintenance` (downtime inside the maintenance window does not count, default true), `alert_breach` (an alert when this month falls below the target, default true) and `recipients` (extra addresses for this customer's uptime alerts). Leave a field out to keep it. | `customer`, `target_pct`?, `exclude_maintenance`?, `alert_breach`?, `recipients`?, `clear_target`? |

## Tickets and customer portal

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list_tickets` | 🟢 read | `read` | Tickets that customers reported in the customer portal (or staff on their behalf), newest activity first, with status (new, open, waiting_customer, on_hold, resolved, closed), priority, linked machines, assignee, whether the customer waits for a reply (needs_reply) and the verdict of the first automatic diagnosis. status: active (the default: everything not resolved or closed), one status, or empty for all. assignee: a username, "me" (the token's user) or "none". query searches subject, reporter, messages and the ticket number. | `customer`?, `status`?, `assignee`?, `query`? |
| `get_ticket` | 🟢 read | `read` | One ticket (id, number or "#1042") with the whole conversation (customer messages, replies, internal notes and status changes), the linked machines, the customer's notes, maintenance window and SLA, and the first automatic diagnosis of the linked machines (findings per machine, failed services, recent errors, open alerts, uptime checks that are down, suggested next steps). Start here when asked to look at a ticket; dig deeper with diagnose_server, diagnose_workstation, search_logs or find_errors. | `ticket` |
| `diagnose_ticket` | 🟢 read | `logs` | Run the first diagnosis of a ticket again, now, and return it: diagnose_server or diagnose_workstation on every linked machine (find_errors on all servers of the customer when no machine is linked), plus open alerts and uptime checks that are down. Takes up to 90 seconds. | `ticket` |
| `reply_ticket` | 🟠 change | `tickets` | Reply on a ticket. internal=false: the customer sees the reply in the portal and gets it by mail, so show the user the text first and write it in the customer's language. internal=true: a note for staff only (findings, what you tried). status: change it together with the reply, e.g. waiting_customer (you asked the customer something) or resolved. | `ticket`, `message`, `internal`?, `status`? |
| `update_ticket` | 🟠 change | `tickets` | Change a ticket: status (new, open, waiting_customer, on_hold, resolved, closed; the customer gets a mail for waiting_customer, resolved and closed), priority (low, normal, high, urgent), assignee (a staff username, or "none"), the linked machines (names or ids of this customer's machines; replaces the list) or category (problem, question, request). | `ticket`, `status`?, `priority`?, `assignee`?, `machines`?, `category`? |
| `create_ticket` | 🟠 change | `tickets` | Open a ticket for a customer (for example for a problem you found yourself, or one a user reported by phone), linked to machines of that customer (names or ids). The first diagnosis runs on them in the background unless diagnose=false. | `customer`, `subject`, `description`, `priority`?, `category`?, `machines`?, `diagnose`? |

## Documentation and password vault

| Tool | Risk | Scope | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `list_documents` | 🟢 read | `read` | The documentation of the customers: network plans, procedures, notes, contacts, hardware and software pages (Markdown), newest first with pinned pages on top. query searches title and text and returns the matching lines. category: network, procedure, notes, contacts, howto, hardware, software, security or other. machine: only pages linked to that machine. Read a page with get_document. Pages an admin hid from the AI are left out. Passwords are never in the documentation: they are in the vault (list_credentials). | `customer`?, `query`?, `category`?, `machine`?, `tag`? |
| `get_document` | 🟢 read | `read` | One documentation page (id or exact title; give the customer when titles repeat) with its full Markdown text, linked machines, tags, version and its attachments (names and sizes). | `document`, `customer`? |
| `save_document` | 🟠 change | `docs` | Write documentation for a customer: create a page, or change one (`document`: id or title). body is Markdown; with append=true it is added at the end of the existing text (for example a dated line under "Changes"). Every change keeps the previous version. Never put passwords or keys in documentation: store them with save_credential. category: network, procedure, notes, contacts, howto, hardware, software, security or other. machines: names or ids of the customer's machines this page is about. | `customer`, `title`, `body`?, `document`?, `category`?, `tags`?, `machines`?, `append`? |
| `list_credentials` | 🟢 read | `vault` | The credentials in the password vault (names, kind, username, URL, linked machines, whether you may use it and whether it is due for rotation) WITHOUT the secrets. To use one, call reveal_credential (needs an admin's approval for every use) or, better, run_with_credential, which hands the secret to a script on the machine without it passing through you. kind: login, server, network, database, api_key, wifi, certificate, license, note or other. | `customer`?, `query`?, `machine`?, `kind`? |
| `reveal_credential` | 🔴 destructive | `vault` | Read the secret of a vault credential (password, username, notes and extra fields). Every use needs an admin's approval, whatever the policy says, and is written to the vault's access log with your `reason`. The first call answers pending_approval: tell the user and stop. Once approved, call reveal_credential again with the same arguments within the time the approval allows (15 minutes and one read by default) to get it. Never repeat the secret to the user, write it into documents or tickets, or keep it longer than the task needs. Prefer run_with_credential when the secret is only needed on a machine. | `credential`, `reason`, `customer`? |
| `run_with_credential` | 🔴 destructive | `vault` | Run a script on a machine with a vault credential, without the secret passing through you. The script gets it in environment variables: SP_USERNAME, SP_PASSWORD, SP_URL and SP_FIELD_<NAME> for extra fields (bash on Linux: "$SP_PASSWORD"; PowerShell on Windows: $env:SP_PASSWORD). The secret is wiped from the output. Every run needs an admin's approval (the admin sees the script and your reason) and the token also needs the `exec` scope; the credential and the machine must belong to the same customer. timeout: seconds, max 1800. | `server`, `credential`, `script`, `reason`, `customer`?, `timeout`? |
| `save_credential` | 🟠 change | `vault` | Store a credential in the customer's vault (encrypted), or change one (`credential`: id or name), for example after you created an account or changed a password with run_command. A changed password keeps the old one in the item's history. kind: login, server, network, database, api_key, wifi, certificate, license, note or other. machines: names or ids of the customer's machines it belongs to. Returns the item without the secret. New items may be used by the AI (with approval); an admin can change that. | `customer`, `name`, `credential`?, `kind`?, `username`?, `password`?, `url`?, `notes`?, `machines`?, `tags`? |
